text: During the intervals the crowds streamed past his cage on their way to the menagerie, and the few who wished to stop and look at him were pushed along by those behind, who were eager to reach the animals. <break time="0.8s" /> In time he became a mere obstacle on the way to the stables, and the little board showing how many days he had fasted went unchanged, for no one, not even the artist himself, was counting anymore. <break time="0.8s" /> When an idle passerby stopped and joked that the figure on the board was a fraud, it was the most foolish lie that indifference could invent, for it was not the artist but the world that was cheating. <break time="0.8s" /> Many days later an overseer noticed the apparently empty cage, and when the attendants poked about in the dirty straw with sticks, they found the hunger artist lying there, still fasting. <break time="0.8s" /> Forgive me, everybody, whispered the artist, and when the overseer, his ear pressed to the bars, assured him that they forgave him, he added that he had always wanted them to admire his fasting. <break time="0.8s" /> But you should not admire it, he went on, because I have to fast, since I could never find the food I liked, and had I found it, I would have eaten my fill like everyone else. <break time="0.8s" /> These were his last words, but in his dimming eyes there still remained the firm, though no longer proud, conviction that he was continuing to fast, and soon afterward he was quietly buried together with the straw. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the cage they put a young panther, whose noble body seemed to carry freedom itself in its jaws, and the crowds, drawn by its burning joy of life, pressed around the cage and would not move away.
